title: API Consolidation Playbook: single surface for chat, completions, embeddings and rerank
creator: Arjun Patel
description: This PRD defines the consolidated API contract and launch requirements for a single hosted inference surface that supports chat, completions, embeddings, and reranking. The goal is to reduce cognitive overhead for customers, simplify SDKs and docs, and enable unified routing and telemetry while preserving backward compatibility where possible.
goals: Ship a single, well-documented REST/SDK surface that exposes chat, completions, embeddings and rerank capabilities
Ensure parity with current hosted endpoints for critical fields (prompt/temperature/top_p/stop/streaming) and maintain existing SLAs
Provide clear migration guidance and automated compatibility shims for top customer patterns
Deliver observability and cost breakdown in Console per-route and per-model for the new surface
Enable rollout strategies (canary / A/B / gradual migration) with automated fallback to legacy endpoints
scope: In-scope: API contract design, SDK method signatures, server-side routing and compatibility layer, telemetry events and Console dashboards, launch docs, customer migration guide, and integration tests. Out-of-scope: major model architecture changes, Dedicated/private deployment agent changes beyond configuration flags.
out_of_scope: Changing model semantics (generation algorithm) for existing customers
Large refactor of Dedicated autoscaling internals
New pricing model or billing semantics for embeddings during initial launch
stakeholders: Eng: Lina Gomez (runtime), Marcus Yu (API), Priya Rao (SDK)
success_criteria: API is live behind feature flag and successfully serves >= 95% of internal smoke tests
No regression in 99th percentile latency compared to legacy endpoints for 95% of traffic profiles
Migration guide completed with example code for Python/Node/Go and at least two customer migrations validated in beta
Console shows per-route token-level cost and latency within 24 hours of launch
No P0 or P1 production incidents linked to the new surface in the first 14 days after full rollout
acceptance_criteria: API contract documented in /docs with examples for chat, completions, embeddings and rerank
SDKs have new surface shipped in minor versions with feature-flag toggle
Server implements compatibility shim: incoming legacy completions/chat requests route correctly with identical default behavior
Automated integration test matrix covers JSON-structured output, function/tool-calling, streaming and non-streaming modes
End-to-end performance tests include batching scenarios and KV cache cold/warm cases with metrics captured
Telemetry events emitted for each request with model, variant, customer_id (pseudonymized), token_count and latency
Security review sign-off completed and KMS key usage documented for private deployments
launch_checklist: API spec published in docs.redwood.com and linked from Console
SDKs released (Python/Node/Go) and example repos updated
Console dashboard updated with new route filter and cost breakdown
Integration tests green across major models and sequence lengths
Canary traffic routing configured (5% -> 25% -> 100%) with automatic rollback hooks
Support runbook created and SLOs published
Billing and metering validated in staging and end-to-end invoicing tested
Customer migration guide and FAQ published; outreach plan for top 20 customers scheduled
Feature flag gating and emergency killwitch validated
Security & compliance checklist completed and artifacts uploaded to Vault
rollout_plan: Phased rollout behind a feature flag. Week 0: internal team + CI runs. Week 1: selected internal customers and low-risk external beta customers. Week 2: expand to open beta for all paid accounts with telemetry monitoring. Week 3: full public rollout with SDK minor releases and Console defaults switched. Rollback plan: immediate flag flip to route traffic back to legacy endpoints; incident playbook triggers paged on latency or error-rate thresholds.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Unexpected 99th percentile latency regression under long-context workloads. Mitigation: enforce stricter per-request batching limits during canary and enable KV cache warmup probes.
Risk: Breaking behavioral changes for heavy prompt-engineering customers. Mitigation: compatibility shim and opt-in strict-mode; run blackbox comparison tests against customer prompts where provided.
Risk: Missing telemetry leading to blindspots for billing disputes. Mitigation: require token_count and model labels on all requests; pre-launch dry-run with billing team to reconcile metrics.
Risk: SDK adoption friction due to signature changes. Mitigation: provide adapter helpers in SDKs and automated codemods for common patterns.
Risk: Security review delays. Mitigation: early engagement with S&C and prepare standard artifacts (threat model, data flow, KMS usage) ahead of sign-off.
Risk: Console UX confusion. Mitigation: include contextual help and migration banner explaining differences for 30 days post-launch.
open_questions: Do we need a new billing unit for rerank calls or can they be billed as a derivative of generation tokens?
Should streaming behavior be identical across chat and completions by default, or should chat default to streaming=true?
Which model variants require immediate quantization recommendations in Optimize to avoid cost regression?
Are there known enterprise customers that must be transitioned off legacy endpoints prior to public rollout?
notes: This playbook intentionally prefers a conservative compatibility-first approach for the initial launch. After a successful rollout we will evaluate contract simplifications and deprecations in a follow-up project (post-launch cleanup). Keep PM, Eng and Design sync cadence twice weekly until GA.
post_launch_actions: Collect migration telemetry to identify top 10 breaking patterns
Schedule lessons-learned retro 2 weeks after GA
Deprecation plan for legacy endpoints drafted with 6-month window
